newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SACCHI RETURNS BUT MILAN SINK ALL THE SAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SACCHI RETURNS BUT MILAN SINK ALL THE SAME.

text.p: Arrigo Sacchi returned to AC Milan on Wednesday only to see them crash out of the European Cup thanks to a 2-1 home defeat by Rosenborg of Norway that owner Silvio Berlusconi called "the lowest point" in their recent history.

The group D Champions' League match was Sacchi's first in charge since he unexpectedly resigned as national coach on Sunday to return to the mighty club he took to two European Cup triumphs in 1989 and 1990.
It was not a happy homecoming.

The angry whistles and boos that had met him in his embattled final matches as Italy coach again echoed around the San Siro stadium on a bleak night for Milan and a historic one for their unheralded opponents.
Goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi was the butt of the crowd's anger, with fans gesticulating angrily at him after Milan twice let Rosenborg take the lead.

"We lost deservedly and we all lost," Sacchi said. "Its not right to take it out on Rossi. We must not look for excuses. We must turn this misfortune into winning energy. Rosenborg showed that they are a real team in which every player played for the others."
Berlusconi, who took over as club president in 1986, said the defeat was "the lowest point in our luck and in the league since I have been at Milan."
The Italians, who accepted the resignation of Uruguayan Oscar Washington Tabarez on Monday, are ninth in Serie A and have also been knocked out of the domestic cup competition.
"I'm disappointed and saddened," the billionaire media mogul and former prime minister said. "But we have to learn from it and rebuild. We will do it with the right leader (Sacchi)."

Playing against opponents Milan had thrashed 4-1 in Norway, the Italian champions again -- as they had during a 3-2 Serie A defeat by lowly Piacenza at the weekend -- displayed all the backbone of damp pasta on Wednesday.

They had needed only a draw, goalless or otherwise, to proceed to the quarter-finals, but found themselves behind after 29 minutes when midfielder Harald Brattbakk picked up the ball on the edge of the area and hit a left-footed shot past Rossi.

The unsettled 29,000 strong crowd began to whistle at their team and Rosenborg could have made it 2-0 in the 36th minute when Steffen Iversen forced Rossi to concede a corner with a powerful shot on the volley.
French international Christophe Dugarry then hauled Milan back with an equaliser seconds before the interval which turned the tie back towards the home side.
Sacchi pulled his former World Cup star Roberto Baggio off at half time for Christian Panucci and also brought on striker Marco Simone for Massimo Ambrosini.
But Rosenborg, who had to win to go through, found the extra effort and Vegard Heggem headed home in the 69th minute to complete a historic win.
Milan, with striker George Weah suspended for headbutting Porto's captain Jorge Costa after their last Champions' League match, showed little spirit and rarely looked like equalising again.
"Its the most important moment in Rosenborg's history," said the Norwegian club's coach Nils Arne Eggen.
"We played an extraordinary match. It was very hard to play in a situation like this where we had to win."
Teams:

Milan - 1-Sebastiano Rossi; 3-Paolo Maldini, 4-Demetrio Albertini, 6-Franco Baresi, 10-Dejan Savicevic, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 14-Michael Reiziger (16-Tomas Locatelli 65), 15-Massimo Ambrosini (2-Christian Panucci 45) 18-Roberto Baggio (23-Marco Simone 45), 19-Cristophe Dugarry, 20-Zvonimir Boban.

Rosenborg - 1-Jorn Jamtfall; 3-Erik Hoftun, 5-Stale Stensaas, 6-Roar Strand (11-Jahn Ivar "Mini" Jakobsen 89), 8-Bent Skammelsrud, 10-Harald Brattbakk, 14-Vegard Heggem, 15-Jon Olav Hjelde, 16-Steffen Iversen, 18-Biorn Tore Kvarme, 20-Trond Egil Soltvedt.
